title: I Let the Choosing Beggar Keep the Free Listing Rules

parts.text: I listed a free beige sofa on the neighborhood page and watched a woman named Kendra treat it. I am thirty-eight, single dad, patience at the fill line. The sofa smelled faintly of the popcorn we burned during a movie night, which I disclosed. Kendra messaged: hold it, I'll send my husband, it better be clean. I said, first come, curb, tonight. She said, I have kids, you have to be flexible. I have a kid. His name is Mateo, and he was eating cereal out of a measuring cup because the bowls were in the dishwasher. Kendra arrived in an SUV without a truck. "You'll help us load," she said, not asking. I said, "I listed free. I didn't list movers." Her husband, Todd, stayed on his phone. "Can you hold it until Saturday? We're going to the lake." The posting said tonight. "Don't you dare give it to someone else. I called dibs." Dibs is not a legal system. I said, "Then take it now." She opened the cushions and wrinkled her nose. "Popcorn. You should discount it." It was free. "Throw in the coffee table or we're leaving a review." We don't have a store. I said, "The table isn't listed." Kendra photographed my house number. "For the police if you resell it." Then Sam's hatchback pulled up, full of friends and straps, and Kendra stepped in front of the sofa like it was a throne she had paid for.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She photographed my house number, blocked the sofa, and the actual pickup crew just arrived.

social.video_title: She wanted movers for a free sofa — Part 1/2
social.description: Popcorn smell disclosed, dibs declared, house number photographed. A hatchback full of straps pulled up anyway. Would you have held it until Saturday?

parts.text: I handed Sam the listing screenshot that said curb, tonight, first come. "It's yours if you can move it," I said. Kendra blocked the armrest. "I was here first." Todd sighed at his phone. Sam's friend, a girl with a tool bag, said, "Ma'am, you're standing on our straps." I told Kendra she could take it if they loaded in ten minutes without the table. She demanded I vacuum the popcorn out of the frame. I offered her the handheld, the one that sounds like a dying hairdryer. She refused to touch it. "That's disgusting. You do it." I said, "Then it's not your sofa." Sam's crew had it in the hatchback in six minutes, Mateo cheering like it was sports. Kendra yelled about reviews. I posted in the comments, politely, that free listings are not white-glove, and that photographing house numbers over a sofa is a choice. The neighborhood page admin, who is tired, pinned a note about pickup etiquette. Kendra reported me for selling stolen furniture. The admin asked for a photo of Mateo eating cereal next to the empty porch, which was weirdly perfect evidence of ownership. Todd later messaged sorry, she's stressed. I did not reply. The coffee table stayed. We eat on it. Sometimes I smell phantom popcorn and laugh in a tired way. Sam dropped off cookies. Mateo said the sofa looked better leaving than staying. He was right. It still buzzes a little. I can live with a buzz that I chose.

social.video_title: The hatchback crew beat dibs — Part 2/2
social.description: Ten minutes, no coffee table, and a handheld vacuum she would not touch. The admin wanted a cereal-on-the-porch photo. Would you have replied to Todd's sorry?
